note: Register of tabnas runtime dependencies that differ between this repository's ports (tabnas/admin ADR-24). tools/port-deps.cjs fails on a difference that is not listed here, and on an entry that no longer matches the manifests, so the list cannot outlive what it records. Every entry states the ports that have the dependency today, the reason, and the repair.

bnf.reason: TypeScript: ts/package.json floors @tabnas/bnf, the grammar notations' shared compiler, at 0.1.30, its latest release. The floor was set at 0.1.29, the release that bounds its left-recursion elimination (tabnas/bnf#108, #109 and #110), on the maintainer's ruling of 2026-10-11 on alchemy-cli#22; 0.1.30 also bounds what its emitter writes and holds (#112 and #113). Until their releases of 2026-10-13, @tabnas/abnf, @tabnas/ebnf and @tabnas/gbnf took @tabnas/bnf through open peer ranges, so an application that already held an older @tabnas/bnf satisfied them with the uncapped compiler, and a twenty-rule left-recursion cycle in a grammar the command reads then cost exponential time and memory. npm holds a peer to a floor only from a package that declares it, so the floor needs the declaration; translate imports nothing from @tabnas/bnf itself. Go and Rust declare nothing because they need no floor: go/go.mod requires github.com/tabnas/bnf/go v0.1.30 (indirect), and minimum version selection never resolves below a requirement, while rs/Cargo.lock pins tabnas-bnf 0.1.30 through the notation crates.
bnf.repair: Met on 2026-10-13: @tabnas/abnf 0.4.23, @tabnas/ebnf 0.1.18 and @tabnas/gbnf 0.1.19 each floor @tabnas/bnf at 0.1.30 in their own peer ranges, as their later releases do, and ts/package.json floors those three at their latest releases, so this declaration adds nothing. Removing it, and this entry with it, is a dependency change for the maintainer to instruct (ADR-22); until then it stays.

parser.reason: TypeScript: ts/src/translate.ts imports '@tabnas/parser' to build each grammar's parser (new Tabnas().use(...)) and to subscribe to ZON's lexer, and ts/package.json declares it as a peer. The command also compiles programs with @tabnas/alchemy's language, which imports the engine (alchemy ts/src/grammar.ts); since 2026-10-06 alchemy declares the engine as an OPTIONAL peer so that packages taking only @tabnas/alchemy/shared do not install it, and npm does not install an optional peer, so the host that loads the language declares it. Go: go/translate imports the engine to subscribe to ZON's lexer; to build the parser of the grammar whose Go package offers no constructor, feed's (a new engine given feed's defaults, as feed's documentation shows); to read the typed values two modules build (feed's AtomFeed, chess's Database) back from their JSON encoding, and the grammar spec a grammar notation's module writes as JSON text, as the engine's ordered map, so that their members keep an order; to name the GrammarSpec the grammar notations' conversions return, which the shared compiler's serializers take; and to read an engine error (TabnasError) as transduce's parser source reports one, for the documents read as such a module's tree. ZON's Go reader builds an integer no float64 holds exactly as a *big.Int, which no transduce event carries, so the host replaces the token's value with the {"$big": "<digits>"} object ZON's translation part declares (the TypeScript port does the same for a bigint). Rust names no engine type: each grammar crate's make() hands translate its parser, and tabnas-zon's Rust reader builds the $big object itself, so the crate declares nothing, and tabnas-alchemy brings the engine to it transitively.
parser.repair: TypeScript: none is owed. The difference is npm's packaging, not the code; the maintainer ruled it intentional on 2026-10-06 (alchemy's engine peer is optional, so the host that runs the language declares it), and translate imports the engine besides. Go: the import goes away only when every use does: when tabnas-zon's Go reader builds the declared {"$big": "<digits>"} object itself, as its Rust reader does, so that no host adapts it (whether it should is zon's: its readers' forms differ by runtime: bigint, *big.Int, the object); when tabnas-feed offers a constructor, as chess, css, expr and semver do (Make, MakeJsonic); when the modules that build typed values give the tree their parts declare, as proto's ParseValue now does; when the grammar notations' modules give the spec they compile as that tree, rather than as text and a GrammarSpec; and when transduce reads a module's tree as it reads a parser's value, its engine errors included. Undecided: awaits the maintainer's ruling.
